plan.contextChunk: This figure shows two doubly linked lists and a free list sharing one set of arrays, drawn as a shaded three-row table beside three head pointers. At the left, three labeled boxes give the heads: "free" in a black box holding a white 10, "L2" in a medium gray box holding 9, and "L1" in a light gray box holding 3. To the right sits a black panel with columns numbered 1 through 10 across the top and three rows labeled in italics down the left side: next, key, prev. Every occupied cell is shaded to match the list that owns it. The medium gray cells at indices 9, 7, 1, and 5 carry keys k9, k7, k1, and k5, their next entries reading 7, 1, 5, and a diagonal slash for nil, their prev entries reading slash, 9, 7, and 1. The light gray cells at 3, 6, and 2 hold k3, k6, and k2, with next entries 6, 2, slash and prev entries slash, 3, 6. The black slots at 4, 8, and 10 hold only next values, 8, a slash, and 4, their key and prev cells left empty and cut by dotted white rules. Shading alone separates three structures interleaved across the same index range, and the free chain 10, 4, 8 shows that a slot on the free list needs just one link.

interactionPlan.concept: Multiple linked lists plus a free list can share one set of parallel arrays (next, key, prev), with each slot's shading showing which list owns it and pointers interleaving freely across the index range.
elements: head box 'free' (black fill, white text) holding 10
head box 'L2' (medium gray fill) holding 9
head box 'L1' (light gray fill) holding 3
table panel with columns numbered 1 through 10 across the top
row labels in italics down the left: next, key, prev
L2-owned cells (medium gray) at indices 9, 7, 1, 5: keys k9, k7, k1, k5; next 7, 1, 5, /; prev /, 9, 7, 1
L1-owned cells (light gray) at indices 3, 6, 2: keys k3, k6, k2; next 6, 2, /; prev /, 3, 6
free slots (black) at indices 4, 8, 10: next values 8, /, 4; key and prev cells empty with dotted white rules
diagonal slash marks denoting nil
index numbers 1–10 above each column

interactions.teaches: Following next pointers from a head visits that list's slots in pointer order, and the three lists' slots are interleaved across the same index range — shading, not position, defines membership

interactions.label: Allocate / Free
interactions.teaches: Allocation pops the free head into a list and freeing pushes a slot back — only a few next/prev cells change while the record itself never moves in the array
Each next or prev entry is an array index (or nil slash), so hovering a cell reveals exactly which slot it points to, making pointer meaning visible inside the compact table

demo_steps.title: Three lists, one storage
demo_steps.narration: One set of arrays holds two doubly linked lists (L1, L2) and a free list. Slot shading — not position — tells you which structure owns each index.

demo_steps.title: Trace a list
demo_steps.narration: Click head L2: the highlight walks 9 → 7 → 1 → 5, following next pointers with arrows between cells. Notice the walk jumps non-contiguously across the table, threading around L1 and free slots.

demo_steps.title: Read a pointer
demo_steps.narration: Hover over any next or prev cell: the slot it references lights up. A slash means nil — the end of a chain. Free slots carry only a next link, since an unused slot needs no key or prev.

demo_steps.title: Allocate a slot
demo_steps.narration: Press allocate: the free head (index 10) pops off the free chain and joins L1 — its shading flips, free updates to 4, and only the few next/prev cells involved animate. Nothing physically moves.

demo_steps.title: Free it back
demo_steps.narration: Press free: the slot returns to the front of the free chain, its key and prev blank out, and the free head points at it again — slot reuse is just pointer rewiring.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Linked lists in arrays are pure pointer arithmetic: shading marks ownership, heads are just stored indices, and allocate/free only rewire a handful of next/prev entries — records never move.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Left column: three small labeled head boxes stacked — 'free' in italic serif beside a black box with white 10, 'L2' beside a medium gray box with 9, 'L1' beside a light gray box with 3. Right: a wide black-panel table, columns headed 1–10, three rows labeled next / key / prev in italics at left. Cell shading must exactly match the owning head's shade: medium gray for L2 slots (9, 7, 1, 5), light gray for L1 slots (3, 6, 2), black for free slots (4, 8, 10). Free slots show only their next value in white; their key and prev cells are empty, separated by dotted white horizontal rules. Nil shown as a diagonal slash. Keys rendered as italic subscripted k1…k9. White text on black cells, black text on shaded cells. Trace highlights should draw curved arrows from each next cell to the column it references; allocate/free transitions should flip one column's shading and animate only the changed cells.

Scale the head boxes to match the table cell dimensions so free/L₂/L₁ read as the same visual class as the table entries.
